title: Following sequential probability updates
description: You can trace the supplied diagnostic-test model through three observations.

steps.description: TestCharacteristics stores sensitivity and specificity as conditional probabilities. You check that the incoming prior lies between zero and one.
Each result branch forms its total evidence probability from two cases. You divide the disease-and-result probability by that total, with a guard for zero evidence.
The demonstration sets prior 0.01 and test parameters 0.95 and 0.98. You supply the result sequence positive, positive, negative.

steps.question: Does each update restart from the initial prior?
steps.answer: No. current_prob receives the previous update's posterior and becomes the next call's prior.

steps.description: You see the model's posteriors 0.324232, 0.957966 and 0.537631. The final negative result lowers the value from the second positive result.
